changes.what: tests/support/redis.tcl: a client socket to the target logs in
changes.reason: runtest takes no credentials and every target logs in; each socket the tests open to the target's port sends AUTH first, and redis-cli and redis-benchmark log in when pointed at it

changes.what: tests/support/server.tcl: FUNCTION FLUSH before each file
changes.reason: the harness runs it before every file and stops the file when it is refused; an engine without Functions would fail every file on that one command, which unit/functions and tier 0 measure, so a refusal is tolerated there

changes.what: tests tagged needs:debug, needs:pfdebug, needs:repl, needs:save, needs:reset, needs:config-maxmemory, needs:config-resetstat, needs:other-server, large-memory
changes.reason: they need a test hook (DEBUG and its kin), a second server or a server setting a test from outside cannot restore

changes.what: CONFIG SET rollback on apply error
changes.reason: it assumes the test client and the server share a host: it holds a port so that CONFIG SET port must fail, but a server in a container of its own binds the port, moves to it and is unreachable after
it sends RESET, which logs the connection out, and goes on as if no password were set
it publishes on one connection without waiting for the PUNSUBSCRIBE reply on another, so its answer depends on which arrives first; it failed one of four runs on the redis-7.2 reference
the same race as the PSUBSCRIBE test above, with a channel instead of a pattern: it publishes without waiting for the UNSUBSCRIBE reply, and answered ok once where the recording had err

changes.what: BRPOPLPUSH does not affect WATCH while still blocked
changes.reason: it blocks a deferred client and then watches the target on another connection, so what it asserts depends on the moment the server counts the first client as blocked; it answered err once in three runs on the redis-7.2 reference

changes.what: MONITOR log blocked command only once
changes.reason: it sends the blocked command on one connection and the info clients polls it waits with on another, then asserts the blocked command is the first line its monitor reads; which one the server feeds the monitor first is a race, and it failed one of three runs on the redis-7.2 reference
it sizes a replication backlog and reads it back from INFO: the server's buffer accounting, not what a replica receives
its tests are LATENCY MONITOR's records of the server's own event loop, an ops tool no client sends
it asserts that FLUSHDB ASYNC reclaims memory in the background: an allocator's behavior, measured through the server's memory figures
it reads the size of a client's query buffer from CLIENT LIST: the server's own memory management, which no client sees
it reads the server's SLOWLOG: an ops tool whose answer is the deployment's thresholds and the host's speed
